title: Day 98: CNN World Cup Security Assessment Flags CJNG Shadow Over Guadalajara; Plan Kukulkan 11 Days to FIFA Opening; El Sapo Hunt Day 98
detail: Day 98 since El Mencho's killing at Tapalpa, Jalisco (February 22, 2026). CNN WORLD CUP SECURITY ASSESSMENT (May 31, 2026): CNN published a major security assessment on May 31 specifically evaluating risks for World Cup fans traveling to Mexico's three host cities. Published 11 days before the June 11 opening match, the assessment acknowledged Mexico's significant security efforts under Plan Kukulkan while highlighting CJNG's active succession crisis and persistent cartel presence in Jalisco as structural concerns for Guadalajara's four group-stage matches. Security experts cited in the report noted that while organized cartel-on-cartel violence is unlikely to directly threaten international visitors, opportunistic crime, potential narcobloqueos, and the overall security environment of the CJNG heartland represent elevated risk compared to other World Cup host nations. The report reflects a pattern of international media scrutiny intensifying in the final two-week sprint to the June 11 opening — with Guadalajara as the focal point given it hosts the cartel's historical headquarters and is the city most directly affected by CJNG's ongoing succession crisis, 98 days post-Mencho. Homeland Security Today (May 2026) similarly documented Mexico's escalating cartel violence and expanding cross-border threats in the final pre-tournament window. PLAN KUKULKAN — 11 DAYS: Eleven days remain before the FIFA World Cup 2026 opening match (June 11, Estadio Azteca, Mexico City vs. South Africa). Mexico's 99,000+ security deployment continues: 20,000 Armed Forces, 55,000 federal/state police, 188 canine units, 2,100 military vehicles, 24 aircraft/drones, anti-drone systems deployed at Estadio Azteca and Akron Stadium. U.S. special forces continue embedded training with Mexican military on stadium attack prevention and drone bomb defense. EL SAPO HUNT — DAY 98: Hugo Gonzalo Mendoza Gaytán ('El Sapo' / 'El 090') remains at large as Mexico's #1 CJNG enforcement target. No capture, elimination, or credible sighting reported on Day 98. His continued freedom is the single most consequential unresolved security variable in Mexico's pre-World Cup posture. Federal Security Cabinet has reiterated his capture/elimination before June 11 as its top CJNG enforcement objective. JUNE BILATERAL MEETING: The Mullin-Sheinbaum bilateral security meeting remains scheduled for June 2026 — the first high-level US-Mexico security engagement following Plan Kukulkan's operational outcome. CIAGATE FGR INVESTIGATION: Ongoing — two investigation lines (federal jurisdiction invasion + possible treason) continue in parallel with bilateral security cooperation framework. MANZANILLO COMMAND VOID — DAY 22: Twenty-two days since El Chucky's arrest (May 9) without a confirmed successor plaza boss for the Port of Manzanillo — Mexico's primary fentanyl precursor entry point. SUCCESSION BINARY (Day 98): El 03 (confirmed leader, financial wing) vs. El Sapo (military wing, at large). DECAPITATION LEDGER — DAY 98: El Mencho (killed Feb 22), El Tuli (killed Feb 22), El Doble R (arrested Mar 11), El Jardinero (arrested Apr 27; DOJ superseding indictment May 14; extradition suspended May 15), El Güero Conta (arrested Apr 27), El Chipo/Jorge N (arrested May 19), El Cabo (arrested May 7), El Chucky/Manzanillo (arrested May 9), El Checo/Tecate (arrested May 13). Operativo Enjambre: 80+ officials. 47+ CJNG HVTs neutralized since Feb 22.

media.caption: CNN World Cup security assessment — CJNG's presence shadows Guadalajara matches 11 days before FIFA opening; Plan Kukulkan 99,000+ security personnel deployed
Mexico's escalating cartel violence and expanding cross-border threats assessed in final pre-World Cup window
